question.text: Krishna Private Equity LVF received its SEBI registration on January 15, 2025 (PPM filed simultaneously). By which date must the First Close be declared under SEBI AIF Regulations applicable to Large Value Funds?

answer.text: Within 3 years, consistent with the minimum fund tenure
Within 12 months from date of grant of registration OR date of PPM filing with SEBI, whichever is LATER — i.e. by January 14, 2026
No time limit — LVFs may declare First Close at the Manager's discretion

explanation.text: The Logic: For Large Value Funds (LVFs), the First Close must be declared within 12 months from the date of grant of registration of the AIF or date of filing of the PPM of the scheme with SEBI, whichever is LATER. Here both events fall on Jan 15, 2025, so the deadline is Jan 14, 2026. The minimum corpus at First Close remains INR 20 crore (general AIF rule). The Trap: Option A uses 6 months (that's the in-principle approval registration window for Trust Deeds). Option B confuses with minimum fund tenure. Option D is incorrect — all AIFs/LVFs have first-close time limits. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers the same. General AIF First Close timing in SEBI Master Circular: 12 months from SEBI taking PPM on record. For Angel Funds (XIX-A/C), there's a parallel 12-month first-close window plus the 5 accredited investor onboarding requirement.
